citations.claim: energy conserved just before wall impact
rebound speed exceeds approach speed despite e~0.91, showing energy injection
first energy_bound violation after bounce: energy exceeds E0 plus tolerance

counterfactual.change: Changed body 0 restitution e from 0.912790531673785 to 0.0; with inelastic impact the same thin-wall collision dissipates energy and no violation occurs, showing the gain is in the restitution/bounce path.

explanation: Fast circle hits thin (0.1 wide) wall with high restitution e~0.91. Incoming speed ~38.9 should rebound at ~0.91x, but rebound speed is ~41.34 (vx -41.33), larger than incoming, raising energy from ~814 to ~911.9 with zero controller work. Likely cause: wall-collision impulse/positional-correction over-corrects for a thin box at high speed over many substeps (21-22 per step), adding energy instead of dissipating e fraction.
vision_note: The blue circle drifts rightward toward the thin vertical wall and makes contact with its top tip by step 7. No tunneling through or dramatic bounce is visible, so the energy gain is not seen as gross motion but the timing and location match a wall-contact event.
